A software development company is tasked with designing an operating system for three different environments: Client A wants an operating system for a small device like a smart sensor. They need it to be fast and efficient and are okay if it's hard to update or modify. Client B is building a reliable server system where crashes must be avoided. They want different parts of the OS to run separately so that a failure in one does not crash the whole system. Client C needs a flexible desktop OS where they can add or remove features like drivers at any time, even while the system is running. i. Identify the best OS design for each client. Give the architecture and explain why each one is the best choice. (6 marks)
[same stem as 1a] ii. List advantages and disadvantage of each OS design mentioned above. (4 marks)

A banking transaction system handles thousands of operations per second. Consider the following sequence of events for a single transaction process in the OS: The process is created to handle a customer's request. It waits for user authentication data from the network. Once data arrives, it performs verification using the CPU. During verification, a high-priority fraud detection process pre-empts it. After resuming, it accesses the database to fetch account details. Due to a database lock, it must wait until the resource becomes available. Finally, it completes the transaction and terminates. i. Draw the Process State Diagram and trace the exact state transitions for the above scenario. (7 marks)
ii. Suppose a process is waiting for an I/O device and the I/O completes explain step-by-step what happens to the process's state and how the PCB is updated (3 marks)

An Indian university in Chennai plans to deploy a secure, network-enabled Learning Management System (LMS) hosted on centralized servers to support simultaneous video lectures, online examinations, and real-time collaboration for thousands of students. The LMS runs on top of an Operating System that must ensure high performance, strong security, and reliability, while allowing easy maintenance and future upgrades. As an Operating System designer responsible for the server-side platform, answer the following: a) Identify and explain the core functionalities of the Operating System required to support this LMS deployment. (2.5 Marks)
[stem as in 1a] b) Select a suitable Operating System structuring method (monolithic, layered, modular, or micro-kernel) for the server environment and justify your choice. (2.5 Marks)
[stem as in 1a] c) Explain how the Operating System manages processes and system resources to efficiently support multimedia streaming and network communication. (2.5 Marks)
[stem as in 1a] d) Discuss how security, networking, and multimedia requirements influence the design decisions of the Operating System in this scenario. (2.5 Marks)

VIT's student OS designer team has developed their own version of Linux and plans to validate the efficiency of their Operating System by executing multiple independent computational tasks concurrently. To demonstrate process creation and synchronization, the Operating System uses a parent process to create child processes and waits for their completion before proceeding. To help the VIT's student developer team, write a C program using fork() and wait() that performs the following: The program reads an integer N from the user. The parent process then creates two child processes, where Child Process 1 computes and displays the sum of the first N natural numbers, and Child Process 2 computes and displays the factorial of N. The parent process must wait for both child processes to complete execution using the wait() system call. After both child processes terminate, the parent process prints its own Process ID (PID), the PIDs of both child processes, and a message confirming successful synchronization using wait(). The program should also properly handle invalid input and process creation failure. Your answer must include a sample execution demonstrating the input and output of the program.

Write a C program using pthreads to create three threads for a Smart Hospital System. The main program should read: Number of patients registered; Total billing amount. The threads should perform the following tasks: Thread 1 - Patient Registration: Display the number of registered patients; Thread 2 - Billing Process: Display the billing amount and process it; Thread 3 - Lab Report Processing: Simulate preparation of lab reports. Each thread must print a start message, use sleep() to simulate processing, and print a completion message. The main thread must wait for all threads and finally print: "All hospital services have been completed."
